items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I was right there to see Mr. Morton.

ctx.x: Did they have any music in school? They didn't have any music in school. You had to pick it up on your own. I just wanted to check on that one point. Let's see, we've gotten into brass band. We've gotten you out to organizing your own young tuxedo. You've had that ever since you organized it. Was that before the depression? That you organized the young tuxedo? Young tuxedo? Yeah. After the depression. It was after the depression. You were playing in the WPA band at the time?

I was playing in the WPA band. I wasn't playing in my band. I was playing in WPA band three years. But on the WPA I was working. One client, one client player, one more. I was right there to see Mr. Morton.

I was staying there three years. I see. And how long had your young tuxedo been going when you joined up with the WPA? Oh, mine and my band were by the WPA. It came after the WPA. It came after the WPA. It came after the WPA. I see. I think so. Well, who was Mr. Martinez?
